schemes.official_name: Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY)
schemes.issuing_authority: National Health Authority, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India
schemes.summary: Publicly funded health assurance: cashless secondary and tertiary hospitalisation for eligible families at empanelled public and private hospitals across India.
schemes.intended_beneficiaries: Families identified as eligible from the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) 2011 data — described officially as the poorest 40% of the population — and groups added by later expansions.
schemes.benefit_unit: per family per year, shared by all members (floater)

benefit_details.text: Annual cover of up to ₹5 lakh per entitled family for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation.
Cashless treatment at the point of care in empanelled public and private hospitals.
Covers up to 3 days of pre-hospitalisation and up to 15 days of post-hospitalisation expenses, including diagnostics and medicines.
Assistance is package-based: the scheme pays the hospital a pre-defined rate for the approved package.

Reference rate for angioplasty in HBP 2.1: procedure price ₹40,600; total package ₹49,300–₹66,700 with bare-metal stents and ₹72,200–₹1,35,400 with drug-eluting stents, depending on the number of stents. Rates are revised over time and some states set their own.
Treatment is portable: beneficiaries can use empanelled hospitals in other states.

schemes.patient_costs_note: ₹5 lakh is a yearly ceiling shared by the family, not money paid to you. Treatment at non-empanelled hospitals, items outside the approved package, and care that was not pre-authorised may not be covered. Ask the hospital's Ayushman desk what the package includes before admission.
schemes.application_channel: Check beneficiary status and get an Ayushman card online or at an empanelled hospital's Ayushman desk; the hospital then seeks pre-authorisation for treatment.

application_steps.text: Check whether the family is listed as a beneficiary on the official NHA beneficiary portal, or ask at an empanelled hospital's Ayushman desk.
Carry the Ayushman card and a valid photo ID to an empanelled hospital.
At admission the treating doctor raises a pre-authorisation under the relevant package code and identity is verified at the Ayushman Bharat counter; the scheme approves the package.
At discharge identity is verified again and the hospital closes the claim with the scheme. (Process as described by AIIMS Bhubaneswar; other hospitals may differ in detail.)

uncertainty_notes: Whether a particular family is a beneficiary can only be confirmed against the official database.
Package rates are revised periodically (HBP versions) and some states set their own rates.
pmjay.gov.in and beneficiary.nha.gov.in are official NHA domains, but our automated check on 2026-10-29 could not read their pages.

schemes.official_name: AB PM-JAY coverage for senior citizens aged 70 years and above
schemes.issuing_authority: National Health Authority, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India
schemes.summary: Everyone aged 70 or older is eligible for AB PM-JAY cover regardless of income, through a separate card for senior citizens.
schemes.intended_beneficiaries: All citizens aged 70 years and above, irrespective of socio-economic status.
schemes.benefit_unit: per year — on a family basis for seniors not already covered; as an exclusive top-up for the senior if the family is already covered

benefit_details.text: Free health cover of up to ₹5 lakh per year.
If the family is already covered under AB PM-JAY, the senior gets an additional top-up of up to ₹5 lakh per year for themselves, not shared with family members under 70.
Seniors in families not already covered get up to ₹5 lakh per year on a family basis.
Care is cashless at empanelled hospitals, with the scheme paying the hospital for approved packages.

schemes.patient_costs_note: The amount is a yearly ceiling, not a payment to the patient. Items outside the approved package or care at non-empanelled hospitals may not be covered.
schemes.application_channel: Enrol the senior for the separate AB PM-JAY senior-citizen card, then use it at an empanelled hospital.

application_steps.text: Enrol the senior citizen for the new, distinct AB PM-JAY card issued to people aged 70 and above.
Take the card and ID to an empanelled hospital's Ayushman desk; the hospital seeks pre-authorisation for the treatment package.

uncertainty_notes: Media reports call the card 'Ayushman Vay Vandana'; the official release we verified describes it as 'a new distinct card'.
The enrolment documents were not listed in the sources we could verify.

schemes.official_name: Integrated Ayushman Bharat – PM-JAY and Mahatma Jyotirao Phule Jan Arogya Yojana (MJPJAY)
schemes.issuing_authority: Government of Maharashtra (State Health Assurance Society), with the National Health Authority
schemes.summary: Maharashtra's combined scheme: cashless treatment for listed health benefit packages at network hospitals, open to nearly all families in the state.
schemes.intended_beneficiaries: Category A: yellow, AAY, Annapurna and orange ration-card holders and PM-JAY households. Category B: white ration-card holders (including government employees) and families without a ration card who hold a Maharashtra domicile certificate. Category C: listed institutional groups such as ashram-school students, children in orphanages, residents of old-age homes, journalists and registered construction workers from outside Maharashtra. Separate categories cover road-accident victims and certain Karnataka border villages.
schemes.benefit_unit: per family per year, floater (categories A, B, C and E)

benefit_details.text: Up to ₹5 lakh per family per year on a floater basis.
Runs in assurance mode: the State Health Assurance Society pays network hospitals directly. The package covers treatment from admission to discharge, including complications.
1,356 health benefit packages across 34 specialties, plus follow-up packages.
Packages include one-time transport, and transport of the body if the patient dies.

schemes.patient_costs_note: The ₹5 lakh is a family ceiling, not a payment to you. Procedures outside the listed packages and non-network hospitals are not covered by the scheme.
schemes.application_channel: Through the Arogyamitra (scheme help desk) at any network hospital.

application_steps.text: Go to a network hospital and contact the Arogyamitra.
Show the Ayushman card or a qualifying ration card — or, for Category B without a ration card, a domicile or Tahsildar certificate with a self-declaration — along with ID proof.
The hospital registers the patient on the scheme's portal and treatment proceeds cashless. In an emergency, the hospital can be informed by phone or email.

helpdesk.text: The scheme runs a dedicated call centre for information and grievances; the number was not listed in the sources we could verify.

uncertainty_notes: Facts come from a government medical college's published summary; the scheme's own portal (jeevandayee.gov.in) could not be read by our checker.
An older page on jeevandayee.gov.in still describes the earlier ₹1.5 lakh scheme. That is historical and is not used here.
Whether a specific procedure is among the 1,356 packages was not verified.

schemes.official_name: Umbrella Scheme of Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi (RAN)
schemes.issuing_authority: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India
schemes.summary: One-time financial assistance for poor patients with major life-threatening diseases who are treated at government hospitals.
schemes.intended_beneficiaries: Patients from families living below the threshold poverty line with a major life-threatening disease (such as heart, kidney, liver or cancer conditions), treated at a government hospital or institute.
schemes.benefit_unit: one-time assistance (up to ₹20 lakh under the rare-disease component)

benefit_details.text: One-time financial assistance of up to ₹15 lakh; up to ₹20 lakh under the rare-disease component.
Assistance is released to the treating government hospital, not paid to the patient.
At AIIMS Bhubaneswar, a sanction order with the amount and validity period goes to the hospital, with a copy to the applicant.

schemes.patient_costs_note: This is a one-time grant up to the sanctioned amount for treatment at the government hospital. Costs beyond the sanction, or treatment elsewhere, are not covered.
schemes.application_channel: Through the treating government hospital (Medical Superintendent's office or the RAN nodal officer).

application_steps.text: Get a treatment cost estimate from the treating government hospital.
Submit the application form with the estimate and documents; it is countersigned by the Medical Superintendent.
The hospital's committee approves it, or the nodal officer forwards it to the Ministry, depending on the route. The sanction is issued to the hospital.

uncertainty_notes: The 2019 RAN guidelines on mohfw.gov.in could not be read by our checker; limits come from a 2022 Lok Sabha reply and AIIMS Bhubaneswar's scheme page.
An older MoHFW page mentions ₹2 lakh per case; this appears to predate the umbrella scheme and is not used.
There is no patient-facing online application link we could verify.

schemes.official_name: Health Minister's Cancer Patient Fund (HMCPF), under the Umbrella Scheme of RAN
schemes.issuing_authority: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India
schemes.summary: One-time financial assistance for cancer patients from families below the poverty line, for treatment at government cancer institutions.
schemes.intended_beneficiaries: Cancer patients living below the State/UT-wise poverty line, treated at a Regional Cancer Centre, Tertiary Care Cancer Centre, State Cancer Institute or another government hospital with cancer treatment facilities.

benefit_details.text: One-time financial assistance of up to ₹15 lakh.
For treatment at RCCs, TCCCs, State Cancer Institutes and other government hospitals or institutes with cancer treatment facilities.
Under the RAN umbrella, assistance is released to the treating hospital.

schemes.patient_costs_note: A one-time grant up to the sanctioned amount, paid to the treating government institution. It is not a cash payment to the patient.
schemes.application_channel: Through the treating government cancer institution.

application_steps.text: Ask the medical social worker or scheme desk at the treating government cancer hospital about HMCPF assistance and the documents they need.

uncertainty_notes: The application process and document list for HMCPF were not available in the sources we could verify.
We have not verified which specific hospitals currently process HMCPF applications.

schemes.summary: Financial assistance of up to ₹1.25 lakh for poor, indigent patients where free treatment is not available.
schemes.intended_beneficiaries: Poor, indigent patients with an annual family income of ₹1.25 lakh or less.

benefit_details.text: Assistance up to a maximum of ₹1.25 lakh.

schemes.patient_costs_note: ₹1.25 lakh is a maximum, not a guaranteed amount.
schemes.application_channel: Not verified. Ask the treating government hospital.

application_steps.text: The application route for HMDG was not described in the sources we could verify. Ask the treating government hospital's social worker or scheme desk.

schemes.official_name: Prime Minister's National Relief Fund (PMNRF) – medical assistance
schemes.issuing_authority: Prime Minister's Office, Government of India
schemes.summary: Partial financial help toward the cost of major treatments such as heart surgery, kidney transplantation and cancer treatment.
schemes.intended_beneficiaries: Needy people requiring major medical treatment; the fund decides each case.

benefit_details.text: The fund partially defrays treatment expenses. No amount or ceiling is published in the sources we verified.
Central and state government hospitals are on the fund's panel, and the site links to a list of empanelled private hospitals.

schemes.patient_costs_note: Assistance is partial. Expect to cover the remaining cost from other sources.
schemes.application_channel: Application to the Prime Minister's Office; see the official PMNRF website.

application_steps.text: The application process was not described on the pages we could verify. Check the official PMNRF website or ask the hospital's medical social worker.

helpdesk.text: Under Secretary (Funds), PMNRF, Prime Minister's Office, South Block, New Delhi-110011. Phone 011-23013683.

uncertainty_notes: Eligibility rules, amounts and the document list are not published on the pages we verified.
The contact details come from a hospital's copy of PMNRF information, not from the PMNRF site.
